items.text: Sensex and Nifty reversed early losses to close higher, snapping a three-day losing streak, after a wild 1,000-point swing during the new closing auction session on expiry day.
The rupee slid past 95.4 to the dollar as Brent crude surged above $105, deepening worries about India's oil import bill.
US Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2023 and global bond yields broadly rose to multi-year highs, as hot US producer prices firmed up bets on further Fed tightening.
The ECB raised rates to 2.5 percent, citing longer-lasting inflation risks from the oil spike, reinforcing a hawkish global tone.
Wall Street and Asian markets fell in sympathy with the oil-and-yields squeeze, with the Dow down around 300 points.
RBI moved to drain roughly Rs 5 lakh crore of surplus banking liquidity via a 26-day VRRR auction, and used FX swaps to support the rupee.
A Reuters poll pointed to India's August retail inflation hitting a 20-month high on food and fuel prices, narrowing the room for RBI rate cuts.
SEBI's new closing auction session drew fresh scrutiny after today's 1,000-point Sensex swing, with the regulator's chief promising a rework of the mechanism.
Adani Ports and its executives settled separate SEBI disclosure and project-related proceedings, closing out some of the group's regulatory overhang.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra used the Global Fintech Fest to push data protection and responsible AI use among fintechs, and floated tokenising gold.
Brent crude surged past $105 a barrel on unresolved West Asia tensions, the single biggest driver of markets worldwide today.
The ECB lifted rates to 2.5 percent and flagged further hikes may follow, while hot US producer prices raised the odds of a Fed rate hike too.
Global bond yields jumped to multi-year highs as traders priced in stickier inflation and tighter central banks everywhere.
The US added Canadian alcohol, dairy and motorbikes to its import restrictions, keeping trade tensions simmering even as tariff talks continue elsewhere.

standfirst: Brent crude topped $105 on unresolved West Asia tensions, dragging the rupee to a weekly low and pushing global bond yields to multi-year highs. Indian markets swung wildly through a volatile derivatives expiry before closing higher, while the RBI drained surplus liquidity and the ECB raised rates to 2.5 percent on stickier inflation.
title: Oil's surge past $100 rattles rupee and bonds as Sensex claws back from an expiry-day whipsaw
watch: US inflation data and the Fed's next signal on rates, due soon, will set the tone for Friday's global session.
